text:
Maya: quick sync — I'm trying to nail down eviction semantics for Dedicated GPU pools. Proposal: two SLA bands (interactive vs throughput) + soft eviction hints from runtime to operator. tradeoffs?
Sam: sketch out where enforcement happens — runtime admission vs operator node eviction?
Maya: runtime enforces per-request admission/priority; operator controls node reclamation. main gap: how runtime conveys tenant-level urgency so operator can make cost-aware evictions.
Alex: i'd lean soft-scoring instead of hard quotas. gives operator flexibility to balance per-tenant fairness + burst credits.
Nisha: +1. also we should prefer graceful downgrade (route to cheaper model variant) rather than outright reject. eviction should trigger fallback routing where possible.
Sam: agree. we also need a compact API surface: eviction_hint from runtime -> operator. minimal fields: priority (int), reason (enum), lease_id. operator uses these plus node telemetry to compute victim list.
Maya: sketch of proto i'm thinking: priority 0-100, reason in {PREWARM, HEADROOM_PRESSURE, OVERSUBSCRIBE, QUOTA_EXHAUST}. include optional score_components for debugging/telemetry.
Maya: example payload:
```yaml
eviction_hint:
  priority: 20
  reason: HEADROOM_PRESSURE
  tenant: tenant-foo
  lease_id: lease-1234
  score_components:
    warmups: 5
    sla_misses: 1
```
ops-bot: note: current scheduler ignores eviction_hint.score_components; only uses priority and lease age.
Alex: operator algorithm idea: compute victim_score = base - weighted(sum(score_components)) + node_affinity_penalty. evict lowest victim_score first, but never if that would drop tenant below reserved_committed_capacity.
Nisha: metrics we must add: eviction_reason, preempted_tenants, fallback_routed_count, avg_eviction_latency. gate rollout behind feature flag and extend console to show per-tenant eviction history.
Sam: rollout plan: (1) internal POC sim where operator reads hints but doesn't evict, (2) opt-in customers, (3) global opt-in with telemetry and rollback window.
Maya: open questions: how do we surface burst-credit accounting into the hint? runtime knows token consumption; operator doesn't. do we include a burst_credit_estimate in hint?
Alex: include a normalized burst_score in score_components (0-1). operator treats it as a bias not a strict rule.
Nisha: also confirm: can we rely on model-variant fallback being available? need a model-routing contract so operator can signal if a tenant has no cheaper variant -> don't evict.
Maya: good call. i'll add a boolean "has_fallback" in hint and require a small contract in routing layer.
Sam: will write a short RFC fragment with proto and operator pseudocode. acking this thread then follow-up PRs.
Maya: thanks all — i'll ping when RFC + draft PRs ready. :+1:
